#
🎻 PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing
Yiwen Song1, Yale Song1, Tomas Pfister1, and Jinsung Yoon1
1Google Cloud AI Research


PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing. It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams. Acting like an orchestrated team of specialized agents, it handles outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting to close the gap between raw research materials and submission ready papers.
## Key Features - **Multi-Agent Pipeline**: Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation. - **Comprehensive Literature Synthesis**: Automatically searches, prioritizes, and integrates relevant literature into the manuscript. - **Visuals Generation**: Generates plots and supports the inclusion of conceptual diagrams. - **LaTeX Automation

hn_items.title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
hn_items.author: slashdev
hn_items.raw_context:
【文章原文节选】: Google's AI Overviews cut clicks to websites by 40% - RevScope Pricing Docs Blog FAQ GitHub Google's AI Overviews cut clicks to websites by 40% November 9, 2026 Google's AI answers are taking clicks from websites in the search results. In a randomized experiment, researchers hid AI Overviews from some US desktop users. Comparing them with users who still saw Overviews shows that an Overview cuts clicks to outside websites by about 40%. Those Overviews now appear on more than half the US keywords DataForSEO tracks, up from 6% two years ago. The industry's answer, GEO (generative engine optimization), has yet to show a way to compensate for the loss. While AI citations correlate with the same kind of link profile that goes with higher Google rankings, in March AI assistants sent websites just 0.3% of their traffic. Search engine optimization (SEO) still decides whether you can be found, but where an AI answer appears, a ranking brings 40% fewer visits than it used to.
